depth.src: Druon2016: 79+/-8% of time in the first 50m of the water column; bathymetry does not constrain a surface-dwelling tuna - it hunts across basins with >2000m bottom depth

sstC.src: Druon2016 Table 3: large ABFT feeding min 7.5C / max 24.0C

chlMgM3.src: Druon2011 reports higher chl-a preferred for feeding habitat but gives no numeric band; band is an expert estimate

season.src: ICCAT GBYP: Med feeding/western basin May-Sep; Druon2016 spawning favourable mid-May (E) to mid-Jul (W)

species.note: Druon et al. (2016) fit SEPARATE parameterisations for feeding and spawning and the two barely overlap: feeding wants CHL > 0.1 mg/m3 with a high gradCHL, spawning wants CHL < 0.15 mg/m3 with a low one. A single band set cannot hold both, which is why this species carries modes and why the applied mode is disclosed in every response. gradCHL and SSHa are REQUIRED for feeding: without them the model collapses into the SST-only lookup the paper argues against. dSST30 and SSHa are derived by Shaka (30-day SST series; daily zos minus the monthly mean zos), not published, and are marked as such.

modes.label: Feeding, large fish >25 kg

sstC.src: Druon et al. 2016 s3: large ABFT feeding cluster min 7.5C / max 24.0C. The 24.0C maximum is interpolated between the Gulf of Mexico winter 85th percentile (23.83C, n=141) and the Mediterranean summer-autumn 85th percentile (24.37C, n=149)

chlMgM3.src: Druon et al. 2016 s3: feeding clusters have CHL > 0.1 mg/m3, but the paper gives no band, so this EXPERT envelope is a stand-in and carries only 0.05 weight. The documented driver is gradCHL, which is a separate required factor

sshAnomalyM.src: Druon et al. 2016 s3: feeding clusters at SSHa >= -0.10 m (98.75th / 99.5th / 97th percentiles for small / large / undifferentiated fish). Declared higher_better over -0.10..0.0 so the score saturates at the cited threshold: the paper gives a threshold and not a gradient, and inventing a decline above it would fabricate a response curve

season.src: ICCAT GBYP: western Mediterranean feeding season May-September. These are peak months, not a closed gate - bluefin feed year-round and the season only grades how good it is

modes.src: Druon et al. 2016 s3, feeding-cluster analysis

modes.label: Spawning, large fish >25 kg

sstC.src: Druon et al. 2016 s1 describes spawning in "warm, mostly oligotrophic surface waters" and gives NO numeric spawning envelope. This band is an EXPERT reading of "warm", not a cited limit: the upper part of the feeding range, widened, because the paper does not constrain it

chlMgM3.src: Druon et al. 2016 s3: spawning clusters have CHL < 0.15 mg/m3 and low gradCHL. This is the inverse of the feeding requirement, which is the clearest single demonstration that one band per species cannot represent both behaviours

sshAnomalyM.src: Druon et al. 2016 gives a -0.10 m SSHa threshold for FEEDING clusters and no spawning-specific value. The feeding threshold is reused so the driver stays separated from SST, and is marked EXPERT because this is an extension of the fit, not part of it

sstWarmingC.src: Druon et al. 2016 s1-2: monthly SST increase (dSST30) simulates the spring stratification build-up that spawning is associated with, stated qualitatively as "high" with no number. The 0C floor is defensible because cooling is not the documented condition; the 2.5C top is this app's assumption about Mediterranean spring warming. The factor is derived from a 30-day SST series, not observed

season.src: Druon et al. 2016 abstract: spawning from mid-May in the eastern basin, to mid-July in the western with a June peak. Not a closed gate - spawning runs through the season

modes.src: Druon et al. 2016 abstract and s3, spawning-cluster analysis

unscorableRequirements: Small-fish (<=25 kg) thermal envelope: Druon et al. 2016 s3 fits it separately at 13.0-26.1C (13.0C from regional expertise close to the western-Mediterranean winter minimum, 26.1C as the 97th percentile of n=2105). The pilot parameterises large fish only, so ?sizeClass=small is refused with insufficient_data rather than answered with the large-fish band.

evidence.citation: Druon et al. 2016, PLoS ONE 11(3):e0150152 - Spatial and temporal characteristics of Atlantic bluefin tuna spawning grounds in the western Mediterranean
evidence.usedFor: feeding and spawning thermal envelopes, CHL and SSHa requirements, dSST30, size split

evidence.citation: Druon et al. 2011, Prog. Oceanogr. 90:1-12 - Tracers of the habitat of Atlantic bluefin tuna (gradCHL as the food-availability proxy)
evidence.usedFor: why the chlorophyll-a GRADIENT, not concentration, is the required feeding factor

evidence.citation: Walli et al. 2009 via Druon et al. 2016 - 79 +/- 8 % of time in the first 50 m
evidence.usedFor: water-column depth scope and preferred band

evidence.citation: ICCAT GBYP - western Mediterranean bluefin feeding season, May-September
evidence.usedFor: feeding season peak months

depth.src: Oceanic scombrid living in the upper water column; seafloor depth is not a constraint. water_column scope means bathymetry must never gate or score this species

sstC.src: Warm-water scombrid range. The existing profile already recorded this as 'not traced to a specific Mediterranean citation' and that remains true; no fabricated source has been attached to it

species.note: v1 carried depth at 0.2 weight while ALSO declaring water_column scope. Since water_column species are excluded from depth scoring entirely, that 0.2 was dead weight that silently redistributed into the other factors on every evaluation. The weights are now rebuilt without it. PFZ treats the common Spanish/Maghrebi name 'bonito' as this species; the global SpeciesNormalizer keeps bonito separate for the SoCal pipeline; the two vocabularies are intentionally not merged.
unscorableRequirements: Prey: tunny are pursuers of small pelagics and squid, and their presence is a prey-field question, not a habitat one. Nothing in this build resolves prey density, so this score is a thermal-window estimate at best.
Fasting versus active feeding phases are documented for Atlantic bluefin but not resolved here.

depth.src: Epipelagic to mesopelagic, largely depth-displaced at night. water_column scope, so the 0-800 m band describes the occupied layer and must not gate on bathymetry

sstC.src: Warm-water surface band for a highly migratory oceanic species. Expert tier retained deliberately: swordfish associate with the 18-22 C layer but a fixed surface band is a simplification of a vertical-habitat animal, and that limitation is recorded rather than hidden

species.note: Same water_column weight correction as little tunny: v1 scored depth at 0.2 for a species that is excluded from depth scoring. This is the clearest remaining example of a dead weight, and fixing it changes actual numbers rather than just the schema.
unscorableRequirements: Depth-displacement diel behaviour: the animal is at the surface by day and deep by night, so a single surface-temperature band is only half the habitat. This build has no diel-depth input.
Prey field, absent from this build, as for little tunny.
Oxygen minimum: large Xiphias concentrate in mesopelagic water with low but not hypoxic oxygen; no oxygen product exists.

depth.src: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Ref. 188, 2945: 0-350 m at the edge of the shelf, usually 10-80 m; retreats below the thermocline to 200-300 m in the hot season. Marked water_column because the band is a below-surface range: a coastal spot's bathymetry says nothing about where in the column the school is

sstC.src: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Ref. 2945, 27121: cold-water sardinella, 18-25 C, preferring maximum temperatures below 24 C. The gate is widened to 27 C at the top because Mediterranean summer surface water regularly exceeds the cited 25 C and a hard ceiling would report a false absence

maghreb.src: Ettahiri2003 / Quaatey&Maravelias1999: optimal spawning temperature 18-21.1C off the Western Sahara and on the West African coast; the NW-Med band of 23-26.5C does not apply here

chlMgM3.src: Phytoplankton-feeding planktivore (Ref. 188, 86940) so productivity is genuinely relevant, but no measured CHL band for this species was found. Expert envelope, and explicitly not required.

season.src: Reproduction in the upper layers during the warm months, averaging about 22 C, with a peak in August in most places (Fishes of the Northeastern Atlantic and Mediterranean species account). Mediterranean landings run early summer to late autumn, so closedMonths is EMPTY

species.note: v1 scored this off surface SST and CHL with a hard 20-27 C gate and no season term. The thermal gate is now cited rather than guessed, the depth band is marked water_column so a 20 m coastal spot stops rating the school by seafloor depth, and the real driver - prey density - is named as a blind spot instead of being approximated by chlorophyll.
unscorableRequirements: Zooplankton: it feeds mainly on copepods and larval mysids, and productivity means prey density, not chlorophyll. There is no zooplankton product in this build, so the CHL term is a proxy for a variable the score cannot see.
Salinity: prefers clear saline water, no lower than about 34 per mille, and no spot salinity exists.

Black Sea: the species is listed for the Black Sea but does not spawn there, so one band cannot describe both basins. The Black Sea is already excluded from region resolution, which is what keeps this honest.

evidence.citation: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Sardinella aurita species summary (0-350 m, usually 10-80 m; 18-25 C; prefers <24 C; warm-month spawning with an August peak)
evidence.usedFor: depth band, thermal gate and spawning season

depth.src: Tugores et al. 2011 (MEPS 443:181): adult sardine in the Balearic Sea, <110 m in the spawning and nursery models. The narrow end comes from Schismenou et al. 2014 (PLOS ONE 9(7):e101498): Strait of Sicily 30-75 m, North Aegean 10-50 m

sstC.src: Tugores et al. 2011: adult probability highest at SST 20-26C in summer and 14-17C in winter; Palomera et al. 2007: spawning preference 12-16C, up to 19C in the Catalan Sea

chlMgM3.src: Tugores2011: higher presence probability at CHLA 0.13-1.49 mg/m3 (with SLA 2-10 cm) and CHLA >0.45 to <4.5 mg/m3 in another season

season.src: Sardine spawn Oct-Apr in the Mediterranean (Regner1987, Olivar2003, Palomera2007, Ganias2007) which is the opposite of anchovy. peakMonths tracks the spawning/aggregation season and decays smoothly outside it. closedMonths is deliberately EMPTY: sardine are present and catchable in Jul-Aug, they are just nursery-dominated then, so gating them would report a false absence

species.note: Sardine and anchovy have non-overlapping Mediterranean spawning periods - sardine autumn-winter, anchovy spring-summer (Palomera et al. 2007) - so peakMonths tracks the spawning and aggregation season and closedMonths is deliberately EMPTY: sardine are present and catchable in Jul-Aug, they are simply nursery-dominated, and gating them would report a false absence. This species is the reason byRegion generalises the older single sstCByRegion field: it needs four basins, not one SST number. There is deliberately NO maghreb override: the south Algerian shelf is sardine habitat but the pilot has no cited band for it, and an override that invents one is exactly the failure this mechanism exists to prevent, so the basin-wide band applies and the gap is named here.

sstC.src: Tugores et al. 2011 summer Aegean model: SST < 22C in June with depth < 65 m; Somarakis et al. 2006 gives 17-19C for Aegean spawning

depth.src: Tugores et al. 2011: Aegean June depth < 65 m; Schismenou et al. 2014: North Aegean 10-50 m. The Aegean is shallow and enclosed and sardine there are shallower than basin-wide

eastern_med.note: Aegean: cooler and shallower than the basin-wide band. Both overrides come from the same life-cycle line of work, so they are consistent with each other rather than independent.

sstC.src: Tugores et al. 2011: Spanish autumn 16-18.5C with sea level anomaly 1-5 cm, and 14-17C with SLA -5-0 cm. The two branches of the documented SLA x SST interaction are merged into one envelope because this build has no sea-level-anomaly input to switch between them

chlMgM3.src: Tugores et al. 2011: Spanish autumn CHL 0.45-4.5 mg/m3 - richer autumn water than the basin-wide 0.13-1.49 mg/m3

depth.src: Tugores et al. 2011: Spanish autumn depth < 90 m

western_med.note: Western: the source couples autumn SST to sea level anomaly, which this build cannot resolve, so the two documented branches are collapsed into one band and the loss of that interaction is disclosed here.

depth.src: Schismenou et al. 2014: Strait of Sicily 30-75 m. Sardine also select LOW eddy kinetic energy (<200 cm2/s2), i.e. the quieter, more coastal part of the channel - that half of the criterion is unscorable and named below

central_med.note: Central: the Strait of Sicily band is the tightest and best-resolved one in the literature for this species, so this is a real override rather than a guess.

unscorableRequirements: Bottom-layer salinity: Schismenou et al. 2014 document sardine actively AVOIDING bottom-layer salinity above 38.4 while tolerating up to 38.5 in the upper layer. An avoidance band cannot be expressed as a positive score without inventing a response to it, so it is declared here instead of approximated.
PAR: < 55 E m-2 d-1 selected (Schismenou et al. 2014).
Distance to the coast: < 250 km selected for egg retention (Frontiers 2022 13:956654).
Eddy kinetic energy: sardine select < 200 cm2/s2, i.e. weaker currents (Schismenou et al. 2014). There is no EKE product in this build.

evidence.citation: Tugores et al. 2011, Mar. Ecol. Prog. Ser. 443:181-195 - 3D life-cycle model, European sardine, NW Mediterranean
evidence.usedFor: basin-wide and per-region SST, depth and CHL bands

evidence.citation: Schismenou et al. 2014, PLOS ONE 9(7):e101498 - sardine habitat in the Strait of Sicily and the North Aegean
evidence.usedFor: central and eastern depth bands, bottom salinity avoidance, eddy kinetic energy

evidence.citation: Palomera et al. 2007 - spawning SST 12-16C, up to 19C in the Catalan Sea
evidence.usedFor: western and basin-wide thermal gate

evidence.citation: Gkanasos et al. 2021, 3D life-cycle model parameterisation
evidence.usedFor: spawning trigger: SST < 16C, November-April

depth.src: Continental-shelf neritic range, marked water_column because the band is a below-surface range. Anchovy are the one small pelagic here with a well-documented Mediterranean spawning trigger (SST above about 14 C, spring-summer, Palomera et al. 2007 for the sardine counterpart); the depth envelope is less well resolved and is honestly marked expert rather than cited

sstC.src: Mediterranean anchovy spawn on the spring temperature rise and are present from the summer minimum, which bounds the useful band at roughly 14-26 C. Labelled 'derived' because it is assembled from the spawning trigger and the seasonal range rather than read off a single measured envelope

chlMgM3.src: Planktivore with high productivity tolerance. Expert envelope; no measured CHL band found. Not required.

season.src: Anchovy spawn spring-summer in the Mediterranean, the mirror image of the autumn-winter sardine (Palomera et al. 2007). closedMonths is EMPTY: anchovy are present year-round, they are simply out of season

species.note: Kept deliberately close to sardinella so the pair is comparable in the UI, but the two are NOT interchangeable: the season bands are near-opposite by design. What they share is the blind spot - both are scored off chlorophyll standing in for prey density that this build cannot measure.
unscorableRequirements: Zooplankton prey density: the actual driver of an anchovy fishery, and absent from this build.
River plume and freshwater input: the western Mediterranean anchovy fishery is closely tied to Rhône and Ebro influenced water, and no river or plume product exists.

evidence.citation: Palomera et al. 2007 - Mediterranean sardine and anchovy spawning seasons and SST preferences (sardine 12-16 C, autumn-winter; anchovy the complementary spring-summer pattern)
evidence.usedFor: anchovy season and the contrast with sardine

depth.src: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Ref. 54256: Trachurus trachurus is given as 0-1050 m, usually 100-200 m for the eastern Atlantic. That is a demersal-juvenile and overwintering envelope, not a Mediterranean near-surface one, so the gate is narrowed to 0-300 m and marked 'derived' rather than quoting a figure that would rate a 1000 m slope as prime horse mackerel ground

species.note: v1 had no SST and no chlorophyll band at all, so this profile was scoring the species on depth, wind and swell alone. The cited 0-1050 m figure was left out on purpose: quoting it would make a deep slope look like prime ground for a species that is pelagic as an adult.

sstC.src: Temperate-subtropical pelagic range. Expert envelope only: no measured Mediterranean SST band for Trachurus was found, and it is preferred over the sardinella-style warm band because horse mackerel is the cooler-water member of this guild. Required, because a planktivore with no thermal envelope is not a habitat judgement

unscorableRequirements: Zooplankton prey: the driver of a horse mackerel fishery, absent here.

Demersal-juvenile phase: juveniles sit on the shelf at 100-200 m in the Atlantic, which is a genuinely different habitat from the pelagic adult. One band cannot serve both life stages, and this build has no life-stage input.

evidence.citation: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Trachurus trachurus species summary (0-1050 m, usually 100-200 m, eastern Atlantic envelope)
evidence.usedFor: the depth band, narrowed to Mediterranean and marked derived

depth.src: Neritic-pelagic shelf envelope for Scomber scombrus, marked water_column. Honest expert tier: the Atlantic envelope is broad and the Mediterranean one is not separately quantified in the sources consulted, so this is NOT presented as cited

species.note: Same structure as horse mackerel so the two clupeiform-adjacent pelagics are comparable. Both are explicitly expert-tier: it would be easy to invent a crisp SST band for each, and that is exactly the failure mode this roster is meant to prevent, so the weaker confidence tier is recorded instead.

sstC.src: Temperate neritic range for chub mackerel. Expert envelope, not a cited Mediterranean optimum. Required, because Scomber scombrus is temperate-water and scoring it without a thermal gate would rank a 28 C Levant summer surface as excellent

unscorableRequirements: Zooplankton prey density, absent from this build.
Coscaphyra and seasonal offshore migration: the fishery follows the water mass and the app cannot resolve either.

evidence.citation: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Scomber scombrus species summary (neritic-pelagic, shelf and coastal waters)
evidence.usedFor: guild and depth context, at expert tier

depth.src: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Ref. 26999: demersal, 0-350 m, usually 0-100 m. Widely distributed on the shelf, and a bait fish of major importance in the Mediterranean

species.note: Deliberately NOT requiring depth. The cited 0-350 m range is far wider than the shelf, so a depth requirement would mostly assert that a 30 m spot is fine, which adds a refusal without adding information. Forage availability is named as the real blind spot.

bottomTempC.src: Expert envelope; not a cited optimum. Not required.

unscorableRequirements: Bogue is primarily a forage species: its real habitat is defined by the prey field (clupeids, decapods) rather than by its own thermal or depth tolerance. Nothing in this build resolves prey density, so the score describes where bogue CAN live, not where they will be feeding.

evidence.citation: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Boops boops species summary (0-350 m, usually 0-100 m)
evidence.usedFor: depth gate and preferred band

depth.src: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Ref. 3688, 54220: benthopelagic, 0-200 m, usually 15-50 m. Inhabits hard bottoms (rock or rubble) down to 200 m, usually shallower than 50 m (Ref. 9987)

species.note: The v1 profile had depth 20-300 m with a 50-150 m preference, which excluded the 15-50 m the species actually occupies and admitted two depths it does not. Corrected against the source rather than carried forward. Substrate stays unscorable because no product in this build resolves bottom type.

bottomTempC.src: Bottom thermal band is an expert envelope around the shelf-slope association, NOT traced to a measured Mediterranean optimum for this species. It is weighted so the score responds to bottom structure, and deliberately not required, so an unmeasured bottom temperature degrades confidence rather than refusing the species outright.

unscorableRequirements: Hard-bottom substrate: dentex inhabits rock and rubble and is absent from sand and mud (Ref. 9987). The app has no bottom-type source, so the score cannot see the one variable that decides this species.
Preferentially <30 m in the western Mediterranean, deeper in the east: a genuine regional gradient this build resolves only through byRegion, and no per-region band is cited here.

evidence.citation: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Dentex dentex species summary (depth 0-200 m, usually 15-50 m; hard rock/rubble bottoms)
evidence.usedFor: depth gate and preferred band

depth.src: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Ref. 4781: benthopelagic, to 300 m, usually 20-100 m; inshore on rock, gravel, sand and mud to 200 m in the Mediterranean, moving deeper in winter

species.note: Protogynous hermaphrodite: females mature first and change sex in their third year, so a catch dominated by one sex is a real population signal. The app scores habitat, not sex composition.

bottomTempC.src: Expert envelope for a shelf-slope sparid; not a cited measured optimum. Weighted, not required.

unscorableRequirements: Substrate selectivity across rock, gravel, sand and mud: this build has no bottom-type product.
Winter offshore migration depth is real (Ref. 4781) but unresolvable without seasonal bathymetric behaviour data.

evidence.citation: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Pagellus erythrinus species summary (to 300 m, usually 20-100 m; Med to 200 m; winter migration offshore)
evidence.usedFor: depth gate and preferred band

depth.src: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Ref. 27000, 5222: reef-associated, 8-300 m, usually shallower than 50 m. Adults deeper than juveniles

species.note: v1 said 5-200 m with a 20-80 m preference, which put the preferred band below the depths the source gives as usual (<50 m). Corrected.

bottomTempC.src: Expert envelope; not a cited optimum. Not required.

unscorableRequirements: Rocky reef structure: reef-associated, frequently around Posidonia seagrass beds, and absent from sand. No structural-habitat product.
Marine-reserve effect: depth matters less inside a reserve because protected fish occur shallower (documented for this genus); the app has no protected-area layer.

evidence.citation: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Epinephelus marginatus species summary (8-300 m, usually <50 m, reef-associated)
evidence.usedFor: depth gate and preferred band

depth.src: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Ref. 3589: demersal, 20-200 m. Adults on rock, mud and sand; juveniles in lagoons and estuaries. Spawns June-July off Tunisia, June-August in Iskenderun Bay

species.note: v1 said 5-250 m; the cited range is 20-200 m. The 5 m floor was not supported and let this deep-water species score as prime shallow habitat.

bottomTempC.src: Expert envelope; not a cited optimum. Not required.

season.src: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Ref. 3589 and species sheet: spawning June-July off Tunisia, early June to late August in Iskenderun Bay. peakMonths tracks spawning, not availability, and closedMonths is deliberately EMPTY because the species is present and catchable year-round

unscorableRequirements: Substrate: rock, mud and sand all used, so this is the one grouper whose substrate need is not a hard gate, but it still shapes local density and cannot be scored.
Protogynous sex change at 5-7 years (female) to 10-13 years (male): a real population variable this build does not model.

evidence.citation: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Epinephelus aeneus species summary (20-200 m; rock, mud and sand; protogynous)
evidence.usedFor: depth gate, preferred band and spawning season

depth.src: Cited Mediterranean presence is 0-500 m, reaching 1170 m on migration (FishBase Ref. 51243 and species account). The 30 m floor is a DERIVED narrowing: juveniles occur in shallow water and this build only offers shelf spots, so a 0 m floor would rate a 20 m coastal spot as core conger habitat when the fishery there is juveniles on rocky broken ground. The judgement is labelled rather than hidden.

species.note: v1 said 0-1000 m with a 50-300 m preference, which spans the entire vertical migration range of a catadromous species as if it were one continuous band. The range is narrowed to the part a shelf spot can meaningfully represent, and the narrowing is labelled 'derived'.

bottomTempC.src: Expert envelope for a conger on the shelf slope; not a cited optimum. Not required.

unscorableRequirements: Rough, rocky, broken bottom: the species is a hole-dweller and is absent from sand. No substrate product.

Catadromous life cycle: conger mature and migrate thousands of kilometres to spawn, so local habitat quality and spawning habitat are different places. The app has no lifecycle or river-distance input.

evidence.citation: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Conger conger species summary (Med 0-500 m, to 1170 m on migration; rocky broken ground)
evidence.usedFor: depth gate, with the 30 m floor disclosed as derived

depth.src: Frontiers 2021 12:614675 (Iberian shelf, B-HSTHM 2005-2016 trawl surveys): 100-250 m with a 140-200 m optimum. Gate from Colloca et al. 2014 Table bottom-depth percentiles 28-385 m; supporting 60-160 m holds 73 % of numbers and 81 % of biomass (Morales-Nin & Moranta 2004). Colloca: the conditions recur over the outer shelf and the shelf break

unscorableRequirements: Nursery substrate and settlement quality: Colloca et al. 2014 fit a Trophic term into the recruitment equation and the Iberian shelf study weights bottom habitat structure, and neither has a data source in this build.
Bottom substrate type: no bottom-type source exists, so the profile cannot distinguish a muddy outer-shelf nursery from a rocky one at the same depth and temperature.
species.note: This is the profile that forced the required-factor mechanism. Colloca et al.'s habitat equation is a PRODUCT - Trophic x Depth x SBT x SBCmax - where any term at zero makes the cell zero, so depth + chlorophyll without bottom temperature is not a weaker hake score, it is a different model. sstC is deliberately OMITTED: the thermal evidence is BOTTOM temperature at 60-385 m and transposing it onto the surface would gate out correct habitat. The sources genuinely disagree and both are cited - Colloca finds SBT limiting while the 2021 Iberian study finds bathymetry dominant and SBT/substrate least relevant. PFZ takes the Iberian depth band and keeps SBT as a gate because a 15C bottom limit is the one point both agree on.

bottomTempC.src: Colloca et al. 2014 (ENM): 5-95 percentile SBT 11.78-15.04C, with high-recruitment cells characterised by 13.8 +/- 1C. Gated rather than downweighted because Lleonart 2001 reports young hake absent from the north-western Mediterranean wherever bottom temperature exceeds 15C

bottomCurrentMs.src: Colloca et al. 2014 Table: SBC max 0.034 m/s, and cells with biomass > 100 kg/km2 sit below 0.032 m/s. m/s and not km/h: 0.034 m/s is 0.12 km/h, and a unit slip would silently invert every cell in the profile

chlMgM3.src: Colloca et al. 2014: 5-95 percentile CHL 0.10-0.91 mg/m3, median 0.26, over the 0-5 months before sampling

evidence.citation: Colloca et al. 2014, J. Biogeogr. 41:254-272 (ENM, Mediterranean recruits)
evidence.usedFor: bottom temperature band, bottom current limit, chlorophyll range, depth percentiles

evidence.citation: Frontiers in Marine Science 8:614675 (2021), Iberian shelf B-HSTHM 2005-2016
evidence.usedFor: the 100-250 m depth band with a 140-200 m optimum

evidence.citation: Lleonart 2001 - young hake absent from the north-western Mediterranean where bottom temperature exceeds 15C
evidence.usedFor: treating bottom temperature as a hard gate rather than a soft score

evidence.citation: Morales-Nin & Moranta 2004, W Mediterranean shelf
evidence.usedFor: supporting 60-160 m depth band

depth.src: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Ref. 9987, 54221: 10-100 m, more common in shallow coastal waters; littoral on various bottoms, estuaries and lagoons, occasionally rivers

species.note: One of only a few profiles where bottom temperature is a REQUIRED factor rather than a weighted extra: the 8-24 C range is a cited physiological envelope, and outside it a bass is not on this ground. Mediterranean spawning is winter (Dec-Mar), which is the opposite of most of the shelf, and is left unscored because the app has no temperature-driven spawning model.

bottomTempC.src: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Ref. 4944: 8-24 C; eurythermic (5-28 C reported for the species in culture literature). The 8-24 C band is the cited environmental range, not a habitat optimum, so it is required as a hard gate only where it is decisive

unscorableRequirements: Salinity: euryhaline from 3 per mille to full strength, and estuaries and lagoons are genuine habitat. No spot-level salinity exists.
Seasonal migration: enters coastal water in summer and moves offshore in colder weather, so the same spot is not equally good year-round in a way depth alone cannot express.

evidence.citation: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Dicentrarchus labrax species summary (10-100 m, more common shallow; 8-24 C)
evidence.usedFor: depth gate, preferred band and bottom temperature gate

depth.src: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Ref. 35388, 54890: 1-150 m, usually 1-30 m; found in seagrass beds, sandy bottoms and the surf zone to about 30 m, adults occasionally to 150 m

species.note: One of the most important aquaculture species; that says nothing about wild habitat, and the profile scores wild habitat only.

bottomTempC.src: Expert envelope; not a cited optimum. Not required.

unscorableRequirements: Substrate: seagrass beds and sand are the real habitat and drive spawning success; no bottom-type product exists here.
Lagoon and estuary use: it enters brackish and hypersaline water in spring, which no spot-level measurement can express.

evidence.citation: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Sparus aurata species summary (1-150 m, usually 1-30 m)
evidence.usedFor: depth gate and preferred band

depth.src: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Ref. 12460, 13780: demersal, 0-50 m, usually 0-50 m. A shallow shelf and estuarine species, euryhaline

species.note: v1 said 0-200 m with a 5-50 m preference. The 200 m ceiling is not supported for this species and made deep water look like viable sargus habitat; corrected to the cited 0-50 m.

bottomTempC.src: Eurythermic shelf species; expert envelope only, not a cited optimum. Not required.

unscorableRequirements: Substrate: prefers sand, gravel and seagrass over hard rock; no bottom-type source exists in this build.
Salinity tolerance: enters brackish and hypersaline lagoons that are a real part of its habitat, and there is no salinity measurement for a surface spot.

evidence.citation: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Diplodus sargus species summary (0-50 m, marine and brackish)
evidence.usedFor: depth gate and preferred band

depth.src: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Ref. 07313, 56504: 5-409 m overall but 5-60 m is the main range, with a separate 305-409 m eastern Ionian population. Adults on broken and rough ground and over sand and soft bottoms shallower than 100 m. Spawns May-July

season.src: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Ref. 4845: spawning May to July, eggs and larvae pelagic. closedMonths is EMPTY because the adults are present and catchable outside that window

unscorableRequirements: Bottom type: broken/rough ground versus sand and soft bottoms is the difference between good and poor M. surmuletus ground, and there is no substrate product.
The 305-409 m eastern Ionian population: a depth band spanning both the shelf and the deep population cannot express two populations, and no citation supports a byRegion split for it here.
species.note: v1 said 5-310 m with a 28-200 m preference. The preferred band sat almost entirely in water the cited 5-60 m main range excludes, so the species scored poorly on its own preferred habitat. Corrected, and the deep Ionian population is named as a limit rather than smuggled into the band.

bottomTempC.src: Expert envelope; not a cited optimum. Not required.

evidence.citation: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Mullus surmuletus species summary (5-409 m overall, 5-60 m main range, eastern Ionian 305-409 m; spawns May-July)
evidence.usedFor: depth gate, preferred band and spawning season

depth.src: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Ref. 56504, 07313: demersal, 10-328 m (to 328 m in the eastern Ionian), 10-300 m on gravel, sand and mud shelf bottoms. FishBase gives 'usually 100-300 m' for the broader range, which is set aside here: Mediterranean M. barbatus is fished on the shelf well above 100 m

unscorableRequirements: Gravel/sand/mud substrate: the species is tied to these shelf bottoms; no bottom-type product.
species.note: v1 said 10-200 m with a 50-200 m preference, which excluded the 200-328 m the cited record actually includes. Both mullids also have separate deep-water populations off the eastern Ionian, so one depth band cannot describe the whole species; the gate is widened and the regional split is named here rather than invented as a byRegion override with no citation.

bottomTempC.src: Expert envelope for a shelf-slope mullid; not a cited measured optimum. Not required.

evidence.citation: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Mullus barbatus species summary (10-328 m, Ionian; gravel, sand and mud shelf bottoms)
evidence.usedFor: depth gate and preferred band

depth.src: Gate 1-200 m is the Mediterranean rocky-shore to slope range rather than the full 0-800 m global bound (FishBase Ref. 4570), because a scorpionfish held at 800 m is not Mediterranean shelf habitat. Marked 'derived' because it narrows a cited global figure using a judgement rather than a second citation.

species.note: The global 0-800 m figure would let this species score as prime habitat on a deep slope, which is wrong for a Mediterranean rocky-shore species. The narrowing is labelled 'derived' so a reader can see it is a judgement, not a measurement.

bottomTempC.src: Expert envelope; not a cited optimum. Not required.

unscorableRequirements: Rocky substrate: it is a benthic sit-and-wait ambusher on rock, and is effectively absent from sand. No bottom-type product.
Posidonia and rhodophyte shelter: a real density driver with no habitat product in this build.

evidence.citation: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Scorpaena porcus species summary (0-800 m global bound; Mediterranean rocky habitat)
evidence.usedFor: depth band, narrowed to the Mediterranean with the narrowing disclosed

depth.src: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Ref. 35388, 6302: 0-150 m, usually 10-60 m; sandy and muddy bottoms. 8-24 C, preferred 16 C (Ref. 4944, 107945)

unscorableRequirements: Sandy/muddy substrate: common sole is a sand-dwelling flatfish and is effectively absent from rocky ground, but the app has no bottom-type source. Substrate is not a missing FACTOR (it is not in the weights at all) but it is a real decision variable the score is blind to.
species.note: v1 said 0-200 m with a 20-80 m preference and no thermal band at all. This is the strongest thermal citation in the whole non-pilot set: a measured 16 C preference, so bottom temperature is a required factor here rather than a weighted extra.

bottomTempC.src: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Ref. 4944, 107945: environmental range 8-24 C with a preferred 16 C. The 16 C preference is the one measured optimum in this profile, which is why bottom temperature is required rather than merely weighted

evidence.citation: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Solea solea species summary (0-150 m, usually 10-60 m; 8-24 C, preferred 16 C)
evidence.usedFor: depth gate, preferred band and required bottom temperature

depth.src: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Ref. 51243: Mugil cephalus is benthopelagic; the Mediterranean nearshore fishery is a surface-to-5 m schooling fishery in lagoons, estuaries and shallow inshore. The 0-30 m gate is a derived narrowing of a benthopelagic 0-100 m+ range, and is labelled as such

species.note: The important change is not the band, it is the blind spot being named. A mullet score driven by depth and surface temperature while its defining variable is salinity is a score about the wrong thing, and the unscorableRequirements entry says so in the API response rather than leaving it implied.

sstC.src: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Ref. 51243, 27121: euryhaline and eurythermal, tolerant of 8-30 C; the wide gate is a real physiological range, and the 18-26 C preferred band reflects the warm-season feeding aggregation rather than a strict optimum. NOT required: mullet are famously hardy and refusing them outside a narrow band would be wrong

season.src: Warm-season nearshore feeding aggregation. Expert tier: the seasonal pattern is real but was not traced to a specific Mediterranean spawning paper, and it is kept light in the weights because of that

unscorableRequirements: Salinity is the single most important variable for this species: grey mullet is a true euryhaline andagroup the profitable fishery is in lagoons and estuaries at salinities from near-fresh to hypersaline. There is no surface salinity measurement in this build, so the most decision-relevant requirement of this species is entirely invisible to the score.
Substrate: it feeds on periphyton and benthic diatoms scraped off hard surfaces, so bottom type matters and no product resolves it.
Lagoon versus open coast: the profile cannot tell the two apart, and they are different fisheries.

evidence.citation: FishBase (Froese & Pauly, FishBase.org) Mugil cephalus species summary (benthopelagic; euryhaline and eurythermal)
evidence.usedFor: guild, depth context and the wide thermal gate

depth.src: Guerra et al. 2015 (Fish Res, Rias Baixas / Cies): preference for spawning on hard bottom substrate at moderate depth, ~20m, with protection proposed for the 5-30m band; Otero et al. 2005: exploited from 5-7m to a maximum of 150m

season.src: Garofalo et al. 2010 (ICES J Mar Sci, Strait of Sicily): peak spawning in spring/summer with peak recruitment in autumn; FAO: Mediterranean spawning March-October, peaking spring to early summer

unscorableRequirements: Hard bottom substrate: Guerra et al. 2015 record a "noteworthy preference for spawning in areas with hard bottom substrate", with dens in crevices (Hanlon & Messenger 1996; Mangold 1983). This is the single strongest predictor of spawning dens and there is no bottom-type source, so a high spawning PFZ does NOT mean suitable ground was found. It is named rather than dropped because this gap is what decides the outcome.
Surface dissolved oxygen: Guerra et al. 2015 report occurrence varying with bottom temperature, bottom substrate, surface DO, surface CHL-a and coarse sediment. DO has no data source here.

Site fidelity: Mereu et al. 2015 report recapture within 1 km in 84-86 % of cases. Not scorable, but it means a spawning "zone" for this species is a site rather than a drifting patch - roughly a 1 km radius, not a 20 km polygon, which constrains the later GPX work.
species.note: A cephalopod whose documented spawning behaviour is the OPPOSITE of where the fish are. v1 scored octopus on one depth band and no temperature at all, which is a statement about being in the water column rather than about octopus. The two modes are deliberately different: spawning compresses to 2-40 m with a spring-summer season, foraging runs 5-200 m year-round. The chlorophyll band is declared as a band, not a monotonic curve, because the source relationship is genuinely non-monotonic.

modes.label: Foraging / exploited

depth.src: Guerra et al. 2015 review: fished 20-200 m in the NE Atlantic and Mediterranean; Mereu et al. 2015 (mark-recapture, 1604 specimens, Sardinia) gives 20-50 m for the trap fishery; Dridi et al. 2023 (six-year GAM, southern Morocco) gives 18-111 m with a 40-60 m juvenile peak

sstC.src: Dridi et al. 2023: highest juvenile abundance at SST 20.7-21C. That is a juvenile-recruitment GAM, not an adult thermal envelope, so this band is EXPERT and is centred on the paper's optimum rather than citing a range it never states

chlMgM3.src: Dridi et al. 2023, autumn GAM: NON-MONOTONIC relationship with chlorophyll - negative below 2.5 mg/m3, positive above. A band is the closest honest shape to that U, and it is declared as a band rather than smoothed into a monotonic curve

modes.src: Dridi et al. 2023; Mereu et al. 2015; Guerra et al. 2015

modes.label: Spawning / den habitat

depth.src: Guerra et al. 2015, Prog. Oceanogr. 129:36-47 (93 visual censuses, 123.69 ha, Cies Islands): spawning at ~20 m with protection proposed for the 5-30 m band. Spawning depth is NOT the foraging depth - v1 used one band for both

sstC.src: As foraging. No spawning-specific thermal envelope is published for this species, so the band is carried over and marked EXPERT rather than invented separately

season.src: Garofalo et al. 2010 (ICES J. Mar. Sci. 67:1363-1371, Strait of Sicily 1994-2008): spawning March-October, peaking spring to early summer, with recruitment in autumn

modes.src: Guerra et al. 2015; Garofalo et al. 2010

evidence.citation: Guerra et al. 2015, Prog. Oceanogr. 129:36-47 - 93 visual censuses, Cies Islands
evidence.usedFor: spawning depth ~20 m, 5-30 m protect band, hard-substrate preference, 20-200 m range

evidence.citation: Mereu et al. 2015, mark-recapture, 1604 specimens, Sardinia
evidence.usedFor: 20-50 m trap-fishery depth and <1 km site fidelity

evidence.citation: Dridi et al. 2023, six-year GAM, southern Morocco
evidence.usedFor: juvenile depth 18-111 m, SST optimum ~21C, non-monotonic CHL response

evidence.citation: Garofalo et al. 2010, ICES J. Mar. Sci. 67:1363-1371, Strait of Sicily 1994-2008
evidence.usedFor: spawning season and the SST-at-hatching recruitment link

depth.src: Eriksen et al. 2015 (FAO, Cephalopod biology and fisheries in Europe II): subtidal to 200 m but most abundant in the upper 100 m; shell implosion at 150-200 m limits large animals. Guerra et al. 2015: preferential spawning depth 8-13 m

sstC.src: Eriksen et al. 2015 (FAO): temperature limits 10-30C; below 10C the animal is inactive, stops feeding and dies within days (Richard 1971, Bettencourt 2000). Unlike the demersal fishes, this range genuinely describes the water the animal occupies, because cuttlefish are shallow-water and benthic within the photic zone

season.src: Eriksen et al. 2015 (FAO): semi-continuous Mediterranean spawning with a March-June peak; Turkish coast Feb-Jun and Adriatic intensification Apr-Aug also reported. Inshore migration to spawn in spring/summer, offshore to feed in autumn/winter

unscorableRequirements: Spawning substrate and egg-laying habitat: the single most important requirement for this species, and there is no substrate product.
Cuttlebone deposition site quality, same reason.

Bottom temperature: a 10-30 C physiological limit applies to the water the animal sits in, which at these shallow depths is close enough to surface SST to be scored honestly by sst. This is the one demersal/cephalopod profile where a surface-anchored thermal gate is defensible, and it is stated rather than assumed.
species.note: Kept its existing cited bands, which were already sound, and given the v2 treatment it was missing: an explicit required factor and an evidence list. The 10 C floor is a real physiological limit rather than a preference artefact, which is what justifies making sst required for this species and not for the demersal fishes.

evidence.citation: Eriksen et al. 2015, FAO - Cephalopod biology and fisheries in Europe II (10-30 C temperature limits; semi-continuous Mediterranean spawning, Mar-Jun peak)
evidence.usedFor: thermal gate, depth band and spawning season

evidence.citation: Guerra et al. 2015 - preferential cuttlefish spawning depth 8-13 m
evidence.usedFor: spawning depth in the depth note

depth.src: Slope/deep-shelf band for Parapenaeus longirostris. Retained at expert tier: the depth envelope is the one thing about this species that is not seriously in doubt, but the exact numbers are not cited here and are not presented as if they were

species.note: DEPTH-BLOCKED at every existing Mediterranean spot (all are 15-30 m), and now also salinity- and temperature-gated on the Levantine Intermediate Water it actually belongs to. Returning unavailable until deep/offshore spots exist is intended behaviour, not a bug. This is the clearest case in the roster for requiring three factors: the species is defined by a specific water mass, and a score that cannot see that water mass is not a red shrimp score.

bottomTempC.src: Levantine Intermediate Water is a 12.5-15 C layer, and the red shrimp association is with that water mass rather than with a species-specific optimum. Marked 'derived' because it is a water-mass characteristic used as a habitat proxy, which is a weaker claim than a measured preference. REQUIRED, because the water mass IS the habitat here

bottomSalinityPsu.src: Red shrimp are associated with the salinified Levantine Intermediate Water, 38.1-38.5 psu in the cited association. Derived rather than cited because it is a water-mass range applied as a species band. REQUIRED: outside this salinity the association does not hold, and scoring it without the check would rank Atlantic water at 36 psu as prime

unscorableRequirements: Sediment type: Aristaeomorph shrimp are associated with specific muddy/sandy substrates and the trawl grounds are substrate-defined. No bottom-type product.
Trawling pressure and habitat structure: the fishery is a deep trawl fishery and the grounds are not equivalent to the water-mass definition above.

evidence.citation: Levantine Intermediate Water characterisation (12.5-15 C, 38.1-38.5 psu) as applied to the Mediterranean red shrimp association
evidence.usedFor: the derived bottom temperature and bottom salinity bands, both labelled derived

depth.src: Fiorentino et al. 2013 (FAO MedSudMed): full range 120-1300 m, deep-water benthopelagic on muddy bottoms, basin-wide peaks 300-800 m (Ragonese et al. 1997; Politou et al. 2004). The gate is the documented full range and not the peak, so the species is not switched off across water it demonstrably occupies

species.note: The strongest argument for geographic regions in the whole package. A 13.6-13.8C bottom band and a 38.1-38.5 psu bottom band describe Levantine Intermediate Water, which exists as a water mass only in the central and eastern Mediterranean. Scored basin-wide, the band would grade a Ligurian or Catalan slope as prime red shrimp ground on temperature alone - a confident, wrong, expensive answer. The documented ABSENCE is therefore encoded as a region gate, and the Maghreb is gated too because no distribution record exists for it. Separately, every spot in the current inventory is a nominal 20-30 m coastal site, so this profile is depth-gated at all of them regardless of region.

bottomTempC.src: Maiorano et al. 2020, Adv. Oceanogr. Limnol. 2020:9471 (MEDITS 2009-2014 + GAM, Sardinia): 13.6-13.8C, with a basin-wide preference of ~13C (Ghidalia & Bourgois 1961; Yahiaoui 1994; Politou et al. 2004). The gate is widened to 13.0-14.5 around the cited optimum because a 0.2C-wide gate would report the species absent from water it demonstrably occupies

bottomSalinityPsu.src: Maiorano et al. 2020: 38.1-38.5 psu, tightly coupled to Levantine Intermediate Water. Widened to 37.5-39.0 for the same reason as the thermal band. Measured live: 38.51-38.60 psu off the Balearic abyssal plain, above the cited optimum, which is consistent with that being Ligurian water rather than LIW and with the region gate below

mldM.src: A benthopelagic living at 400-600 m is necessarily below the seasonal mixed layer in summer, so a thin one is mildly favourable. No citation states a threshold: the direction is defensible, the 2000 m ceiling is this app's cap, and the factor carries 0.05 weight

western_med.unavailable: Red shrimp do not occur in the Ligurian, Catalan or Balearic seas. Ragonese & Bianchini 1995 and Papaconstantinou & Kapiris 2003 record the species from Sardinia, the north/central Tyrrhenian, the Strait of Sicily, the Ionian and Malta, and its ABSENCE from the Ligurian, Catalan and Balearic basins. The documented 13.6-13.8C / 38.1-38.5 psu band describes Levantine Intermediate Water, a water mass that is not formed in these sub-basins, so local measurements here are in-band at best by accident. This is absence rather than a low score: no measurement could make this a red shrimp zone.

maghreb.unavailable: No red shrimp distribution record exists for the Maghreb shelf in the sources behind this profile. The species is documented from the central and eastern Mediterranean only, and rather than assume that silence means abundance, this region is reported as unavailable pending a citation.

unscorableRequirements: Bottom substrate: the FAO 2020 Aristeidae catalogue and Fischer et al. 1987 record the species on mud and soft mud. There is no bottom-type source, so a rocky slope at the right temperature and salinity would score identically to a muddy one.

Diel behaviour: ascends to shallower depths at night, especially in winter (Cau & Deiana 1982; Kapiris et al. 2010). Not a habitat gate, but it means a score is a 24-hour statement about a species that is not in the same place at night.

evidence.citation: Maiorano et al. 2020, Adv. Oceanogr. Limnol. 2020:9471 - MEDITS 2009-2014 + GAM, Sardinia
evidence.usedFor: bottom temperature 13.6-13.8C, bottom salinity 38.1-38.5 psu, 400-600 m peak depth

evidence.citation: Fiorentino et al. 2013, FAO MedSudMed - Aristeidae, Mediterranean
evidence.usedFor: 120-1300 m full range, 300-800 m basin peak, muddy substrate

evidence.citation: Ragonese & Bianchini 1995; Papaconstantinou & Kapiris 2003 via Maiorano 2020
evidence.usedFor: present and absent distribution, which becomes the western and Maghreb region gates

evidence.citation: Bianchini 1999 via Fiorentino et al. 2013 - Pantelleria Channel
evidence.usedFor: consistently found only below 600 m
